attachments.document_title: Proof of when the landlord learned of the defect (tenant's dated notice, landlord's or manager's acknowledgement, or inspection record)
attachments.label: A2
must_show: how and when the landlord learned of the defect
attachments.text:
E-mail

From: Chris Zimmermann
To: Chris Ellis, Birkenrain Management Ltd
Date: 22.05.2026, 07:48
Subject: No hot water, Mattenweg 133, 3rd floor

Dear Mr Ellis,
since yesterday evening there has been no hot water in our flat on the 3rd floor at Mattenweg 133, only cold water from all taps, and the boiler in the hall cupboard is banging loudly. Could you please arrange for someone to look at it?
Kind regards, Chris Zimmermann

---

From: Chris Ellis, Birkenrain Management Ltd
To: Chris Zimmermann
Date: 22.05.2026, 10:12
Subject: RE: No hot water, Mattenweg 133, 3rd floor

Dear Mr Zimmermann,
thank you for your message of this morning. We have noted that the hot water in your flat is not working and that the boiler is making a loud noise, and we will pass this on to our heating contractor.
Kind regards,
Chris Ellis
Birkenrain Management Ltd

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord does not yet know of the defect (the tenant has not reported it and the landlord has not learned of it in another way)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that at least one rent payment has already been paid into deposit with the office designated by the canton?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant intends to pay the rent on deposit with the office designated by the canton instead of to the landlord, or has begun to do so?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord learned of the defect only orally, so that no written notice, written acknowledgement or inspection record of it exists?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the tenant claim compensation from the landlord for damage the defect caused to the tenant (for example damaged furniture or clothing, or extra costs)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

text:
Good morning,

Birkenrain Management Ltd has known about the problem in our flat since the very morning it started, so this is not a case of the landlord being unaware of it.

Since 22 May 2026 we have had almost no hot water in our flat at Mattenweg 133 in Baar. Some mornings it runs lukewarm for a minute, then it's cold. Washing means boiling kettles on the stove. On top of that, the boiler cupboard in the hallway makes a loud banging noise at night that wakes us both. For CHF 2230 a month I expect to be able to wash at home.

I've attached our lease so you can see what we rent and what it's for.

There is also something about the rent that I can't get to the bottom of. Mr Ellis told me on the phone last week that, as far as he could see, the June rent had not come in to Birkenrain but had turned up at the official deposit office instead. My partner Clara Bachmann looks after our payments, she has been in Portugal with her mother since the end of May, I can't reach her properly, and the banking app is in her name. Whether that money really went to the deposit office or is simply stuck somewhere, I honestly can't say at this point.

I've also attached my e-mail to Mr Ellis of 22 May and his reply. I reported the problem in writing that same morning and he confirmed it in writing, so this is not something he only heard about on the phone.

I'd be grateful for advice on what to do next.

Regards,
Chris Zimmermann
